_why: ADR 0045's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
This one needed a new capability. Its 'suite' is not a test runner -- it
is the guard script `check_findings_reach_a_surface.py`, which walks
every KineticResult field from the resolver, through the runner, across
the Python/TypeScript boundary, to a rendering surface. The verdict is
The harness now supports `"verdict": "exit_code"` for exactly this
shape, and it is deliberately more careful than reading the exit code:
a mutation that makes a guard CRASH also exits non-zero, and calling
that 'caught' would certify a check that no longer runs at all. Crashes
are detected and reported INDETERMINATE. Verified by breaking the
guard's own syntax and confirming the harness refuses to call it caught.

ADR 0100 shares this set rather than opening a second one: G2 IS that record's table, and the two mutations belong together -- G2 only became expressible once the invariant it protects was stated, and G1 is the defect it nearly excused. Two files would split one finding.
ADR 0102 shares it too: that pass changed the fixture, the path matcher and the TypeScript sources read, and G1/G2 re-run unchanged are the evidence it did not quietly stop catching anything.
